The expansion 1/(1 − z) = − z is valid for |z| > 1. What does it imply about the original
n=1
rational function at zero and one?
(A) Both points are essential singularities.
(B) Zero is essential and one is removable.
(C) Zero is ordinary and one is a simple pole.
(D) Zero is a pole of infinite order and one is essential.
(E) Both points are removable singularities.

solution.text:
The rational function is holomorphic at zero and has a simple pole at one. The displayed
Laurent series is centered at zero but valid only outside the unit circle, so it is not a local
punctured-disk expansion at either candidate singularity. Infinitely many negative pow-
ers in such an exterior expansion do not establish an essential singularity at one. This is
precisely where the center and annulus matter.

question.text:
How many distinct maximal annuli centered at zero support Laurent expansions of 1/[(z − 1)(z +
2)(z − 4)]?
(A) 1 (B) 3 (C) 2 (D) 5 (E) 4

solution.text:
The singularity moduli are 1, 2, 4. They give the four maximal annuli 0 < |z| < 1, 1 < |z| <
2, 2 < |z| < 4, and |z| > 4. The innermost expansion has zero principal part and extends to
the Taylor series on the full disk |z| < 1, including its center.
